paper_title: First Searches for Axions and Axion-Like Particles with the LUX Experiment
notes: Paper presents two independent exclusion limits: (1) Solar axions: g_ae < 3.5×10^-12 (90% C.L.), mass-independent limit encoded as horizontal line at [0, 3.5e-12]. (2) Galactic ALPs: g_ae < 4.2×10^-13 (90% C.L.) for masses 1–16 keV/c^2, encoded as horizontal line spanning [1e3 eV, 4.2e-13] to [16e3 eV, 4.2e-13]. Both limits are from profile likelihood ratio analysis of 2013 LUX data (95 live-days × 118 kg fiducial mass). The paper also reports corresponding axion mass exclusions under DFSZ (m_a < 0.12 eV) and KSVZ (m_a > 36.6 eV) models, but the primary experimental result is on g_ae coupling. No local dark matter density assumption is needed—this is a direct detection experiment searching for solar axions and galactic ALPs via axio-electric effect in xenon, not a haloscope. | selector: text over figure_vision (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 0, 0.95, 4))
